title: Decision UIs
description: Dedicated layouts for decisions that used to be a plain list of options. Synthetic gallery fixtures, not captured engine states.

shots.heading: Unexpected Action: recall your token
shots.caption: Each system holding one of your command tokens is shown with its planets, ships and tokens instead of a bare system number, and can be picked on the map.

shots.heading: Predictive Intelligence: restack tokens
shots.caption: The end-of-turn redistribution as pools to arrange, with tokens moved out and in marked. Confirm says how many moves it will send (here 2); the engine takes them one per question, then the plan finishes with 'done'. 647 of these questions were answered as plain lists in the nightly runs.

shots.heading: Player picks (Spy, Insubordination, Signal Jamming, ...)
shots.caption: The card's printed text sits above the options, and each candidate shows their faction, VP, trade goods and commodities; Spy adds how many action cards they hold and Insubordination how many tactic tokens. The same layout serves every card that asks for a player (about 74 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Legendary planet abilities
shots.caption: The end-of-turn (or when-you-pass) menu names the window and shows each ready ability with its planet, resources and influence, and the printed text of the ability card instead of a bare label. Decline ends the window (86 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Manipulate Investments
shots.caption: The five placements use the strategy card grid, with each card's printed text and the trade goods already on it. The header says which good this is (here 2 of 5) and how many different cards are still owed (at least 3 in all). The same trade-goods note now also shows in the strategy phase draft (85 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Letnev: Munitions Reserves
shots.caption: The offer at the start of a combat round shows the ability as printed, the price against the trade goods held (5, 3 after) and one button that says what it spends; Skip declines. It is offered before any dice are rolled and costs 2 trade goods every round (79 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Scuttle and Refit Troops: pick a unit
shots.caption: The printed card sits above the options, and each unit is named with its icon, its system (or planet) and what the card does to it: the trade goods a scuttled ship pays out, or that an infantry becomes a mech. Raw ids like '26|0' are gone (80 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Divert Funding: pick a technology
shots.caption: Each technology shows its colour, the prerequisites it needs and its printed text instead of a bare name, and the header says whether this half of the card returns a technology to the deck or researches another. The same notes appear for Plagiarize, Focused Research and Reveal Prototype (36 questions in the nightly runs).

shots.heading: Riders: predict the outcome
shots.caption: The rider's printed text (what a correct prediction pays, and that the rider player cannot vote) sits above the options, and each outcome reads in words (For, Against, an elected planet or player). It applies to every rider, not only Imperial (31 questions in the nightly runs). The agenda card itself is not shown yet: the engine does not keep which agenda is being voted on.

shots.heading: Exploration cards: choose the reward
shots.caption: The exploration card is shown as printed (name, type and text) above the reward options, so a choice like 'gain 2 commodities' or 'convert up to 2 commodities to trade goods' is read against the card that offers it (29 questions in the nightly runs).
